what: Is the 2% input-gain margin a tuned number or a robust one?
finding: The distribution is bimodal with an enormous gap: every genuine adoption gains 39.6% to 96.4% of its input error, the rejections all lose ground, and e17 sits alone at +0.56%. Any threshold between about 1% and 39% produces exactly the same twelve verdicts.
why_it_matters: The margin is therefore not a tuned parameter and 2% was not chosen to produce a particular answer -- it could have been 5% or 30% with identical results. That is what makes the pre-registration meaningful rather than decorative.
effect_on_what_is_already_on_the_board: None. All seven adoptions in the uploaded Tier 3 v3 entry clear the margin by at least a factor of 20, so the uniform rule does not retroactively invalidate anything submitted. Only e17, which was never in a submitted entry, is excluded.
